title: How to create an AI Agent team with Openclaw and Hermes
description: How to create an AI Agent team with Openclaw and Hermes using the supervisor builder stack on my laptop powered by @snapdragon #ai #tech #SponsoredBySnapdragon #SnapdragonXSeries
transcript: Most people don't realize they can set up a team of AI agents that run 24/7, handle your emails, monitor your socials, and get smarter every time they complete a task. I have this setup running on my laptop powered by Snapdragon because its powerful CPU lets me run multi-agent workflows in parallel. I'm partnering with them to show you how you can do it, too. Install Open Cloud and choose GPT-5.5 as your model because it's the best for agent use. Connect it to Telegram and go to Cloud Hub and choose skills that your agents will use. For me, these include email monitoring, content scheduling, and a content research agent. Install the Hermes agent from Nous Research and use Cloud Sonic 4.6 as your model. The best structure to run the Open Cloud Hermes stack is supervisor-builder workflow. Open Cloud is your supervisor that plans and delegates. Hermes is the executor agent that does the work and learns from each iteration. This means that every time your Hermes agent finishes a task, it analyzes what it did and saves the workflow as a reusable skill automatically. Give your agent team a real workflow with a self-learning loop. Tell Hermes to check your inbox every morning at 9:00 a.m., summarize what needs a response, pull your calendar events for the day, and send you over the briefing on Telegram. The first time your Hermes agent runs this briefing, it tries to figure out the workflow from scratch. Over time, it will start catching patterns that you didn't ask for, including flagging emails from specific contacts as high priority because you always respond to those first. Now, stack the next workflows: a content monitor agent that scans trending topics in your niche and a client outreach agent that drafts follow-ups. Each one runs in parallel on your Snapdragon laptop, and each one self-improving with every single run. I made a step-by-step beginner's guide on how to build the stack out. Just comment "Snap" and I'll send it to you. Follow for more news and practical advice on building with AI.
